Cascade Legal Rights Project takes the concerns raised here seriously. We understand why someone would be upset or frightened to receive a letter from a lawyer soon after asking for help. People should be able to seek information about their housing without worrying that doing so will put them at greater risk.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing clinic attendees’ information to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records are retained internally in locked storage. We also ask everyone here not to post personal details about anyone who may have attended a clinic.

Eviction filings in magistrate court are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for such letters, but we cannot know the source of any particular letter from the information shared here. We will not discuss anyone’s individual situation on this board.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., and everyone seeking help is welcome. The library meeting room is closed for repairs, so the clinic has moved to the Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. No appointment is needed.

If you have questions about the clinic or our information practices, please contact us at clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. Please contact us directly rather than sharing personal or case information in this public thread.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
